examined_formations.title: INDUSTRIAL_UTILITY_BILL_COST_AUDIT
examined_formations.chinese_title: 工业能源账单成本审计
buyer_budget_evidence: A current 2026 buyer offers £2,500 per completed industrial utility audit, guarantees at least £2,500 per month, and explicitly expects multiple recurring client audits.

The bounded audit consumes 6–12 months of bills, contracts, meter/tariff and consumption data and is paid to identify billing leakage, contract discrepancies, demand charges and savings opportunities.
examined_formations.formation_frame: Repeated industrial billing, tariff and consumption-state mismatches create observable cost leakage; the paid audit is downstream evidence that actors already spend to resolve that state.
examined_formations.exact_incumbent_preflight: EnergyCAP currently runs configurable utility-bill audits automatically on bill import, flags cost/usage anomalies and billing errors, assigns review actions and tracks cost recovery.
examined_formations.evidence_summary: The money motion is strong but does not expose a founder-independent operator edge. The machine-detectable audit layer already exists; the higher-value remainder is expert interpretation and procurement/engineering recommendation.

examined_formations.title: COMMERCIAL_BESS_PERMIT_EXPEDITING
examined_formations.chinese_title: 商业储能项目许可推进与主管部门协调
buyer_budget_evidence: A current commercial BESS developer in Texas and Illinois is hiring a permit expeditor for more than 30 hours per week, more than six months, at $15–$35/hour with contract-to-hire intent.
The paid scope includes permit packages, municipal portals, fee payments, code research, AHJ/utility/fire-department follow-up and rejected-comment resolution.
examined_formations.formation_frame: Repeated jurisdictional state transitions between design-ready projects and permission-to-build create schedule pressure and repeated coordination work.
examined_formations.exact_incumbent_preflight: PermitFlow currently markets AI agents for permit intake, requirements research, submission, AHJ coordination, comment handling and issuance across 7,000+ AHJs.
examined_formations.evidence_summary: The state transition is real and expensive, but the reusable workflow is already a current product category. Remaining work is precisely the irregular stakeholder and jurisdiction tail that resists founder-independent normalization.

examined_formations.title: MEDICAL_CREDENTIALING_AND_PAYER_ENROLLMENT
examined_formations.chinese_title: 医疗资质认证与保险方入网
buyer_budget_evidence: A current U.S. RCM buyer is hiring an additional credentialing and payer-enrollment specialist for more than 30 hours per week, more than six months, with contract-to-hire intent and two hires already recorded.
The ongoing paid work covers CAQH, Medicare/Medicaid/commercial enrollment, payer follow-up, deficiencies, rosters, EFT/ERA and recredentialing.
examined_formations.formation_frame: Provider growth continuously regenerates the state transition from licensed clinician to payer-enrolled and billing-ready provider.
examined_formations.exact_incumbent_preflight: Medallion currently offers provider credentialing/enrollment operations with automated payer follow-ups, verification/admin work, portal/email/SMS/fax/phone interactions and real-time workflow visibility.
examined_formations.evidence_summary: This is a durable replenishing actor state, but not an unowned operator layer. Current platforms already automate the standard flow; the remaining value is exception ownership around external payer rules and authorization.

examined_formations.title: AMAZON_EU_PRODUCT_AND_EPR_COMPLIANCE_OPERATIONS
examined_formations.chinese_title: Amazon 欧盟商品与 EPR 合规运营
buyer_budget_evidence: A current Amazon seller is hiring a long-term EU compliance specialist at $20–$50/hour for more than six months and wants continuing ownership across EPR/PPWR, WEEE, batteries, GPSR, CE, REACH/RoHS, labeling and Account Health.
The posting reports one hire and explicitly distinguishes the role from a separate existing VAT provider, proving external compliance spend across multiple rails.
examined_formations.formation_frame: Cross-border assortment changes and regulation renew the seller state transition from product-ready to marketplace-compliant and continuously sellable.
examined_formations.exact_incumbent_preflight: Amazon currently provides EPR policy rails, EPR Pay on Behalf in supported countries, GPSR requirements, compliance reference/tooling and directs sellers to service providers where platform-native coverage is incomplete.
examined_formations.evidence_summary: The money motion is explicit, but the buyer is purchasing accountable regulatory coverage across changing regimes rather than a clean execution primitive. Platform-native services cover part of the loop and the remainder stays expert-heavy.

examined_formations.title: PROCUREMENT_FUNCTION_SETUP_AND_VENDOR_ONBOARDING_RECOVERY
examined_formations.chinese_title: 采购体系搭建与供应商入驻整顿
buyer_budget_evidence: A current multifamily operator with nearly 3,000 units across six states offers a $4,500 three-month project with potential full-time conversion to build a formal procurement function.
The buyer states that vendor accounts, invoices and outstanding balances are scattered and expects systems, vendor relationships, onboarding, cleanup and workflows to be created.
examined_formations.formation_frame: Portfolio growth creates recurring supplier and spend-state fragmentation, but the observed purchase is an organizational recovery/buildout event rather than a standardized routing unit.
examined_formations.exact_incumbent_preflight: Zip currently provides intake/procurement orchestration and supplier onboarding, while Coupa's current Supplier Portal includes structured onboarding, business/payment/legal-entity data and 2026 AI-assisted profile prefilling.
examined_formations.evidence_summary: This is a useful counterexample: even an automation-friendly buyer pays for a human to normalize a messy operating state because vendor relationships, historical cleanup and policy adoption are organization-specific. That is implementation/OCM demand, not clean white space.

examined_formations.title: SHOPIFY_MULTI_STATE_SALES_TAX_FILING
examined_formations.chinese_title: Shopify 美国多州销售税持续申报
buyer_budget_evidence: A current Shopify merchant registered in eight U.S. states seeks ongoing filing for more than six months on a fixed price per sales-tax return, with likely additional states over time.
The buyer explicitly says Shopify Tax is already used for sales-tax reporting, so the external spend is a clear post-native-tool paid workaround rather than mere software ignorance.
examined_formations.formation_frame: Sales into additional jurisdictions repeatedly regenerate filing obligations and deadlines as merchant nexus/registration state changes.
examined_formations.exact_incumbent_preflight: Shopify Tax currently supports automated filing for all U.S. sales-tax states, covering monthly through annual returns, at a published $75 per generated return for Basic/Grow/Advanced and $50 for Plus.
examined_formations.evidence_summary: This is the strongest post-incumbent budget signal in the pass. It proves external spend can persist after a native feature appears, but does not prove an unowned standardized layer because Shopify now directly sells the bounded filing unit.
